item.title: a short note about code review
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
I keep coming back to code review, so here are the notes I wish I had earlier.

why it matters

Code review shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: on code review
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
I spent a while getting code review wrong. Here is the version that works for me.

why it matters

Code review shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.
  • Most of the value is in deleting, not adding.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: notes on code review
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Short post: code review is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Code review shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • Write it down once, link to it everywhere.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
